stem: A insurer's on-premises batch servers upload files to Cloud Storage and query BigQuery over HA VPN tunnels, never over the internet. The security team also runs VPC Service Controls around the data projects and wants the servers to be unable to reach any Google API that VPC Service Controls cannot protect. Which design meets this?

choices.text: Give each on-premises server a public route to Google APIs, then add VPC Service Controls ingress rules that deny any API request arriving from outside the perimeter
Resolve all Google API names on premises to the private.googleapis.com addresses, and advertise that range through the Cloud Router so every Google API stays reachable over the tunnels
Enable Private Google Access on the VPC subnets that terminate the tunnels, because that setting also covers requests that originate in the on-premises network
Resolve all Google API names on premises to the restricted.googleapis.com addresses, and advertise that range from the Cloud Router

stem: After a migration, on-premises clients that use Private Google Access for on-premises hosts show intermittent failures: some Cloud Storage calls succeed and others time out. Investigation shows the on-premises DNS zone for googleapis.com holds an A record for restricted.googleapis.com, but the CNAME and a manually added A record for storage.googleapis.com use addresses from the private.googleapis.com range. Routes and tunnels are healthy. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Point every record in the zone at one virtual IP range, either restricted or private, and do not mix addresses from both
Move the manual storage.googleapis.com record to a public DNS zone so that the resolver chooses the nearest address
Raise the TTL on the googleapis.com records so that clients cache one answer and always use the same address
Add a second Cloud Router in another region so that both address ranges are advertised over separate tunnels

stem: A media firm is allowed to use only Google APIs that VPC Service Controls supports in its regulated analytics environment, but its marketing environment, connected to the same data center, must also call Google Maps Platform APIs from on premises. Which approach respects both rules with the least duplication?

choices.text: Use public Google API addresses for marketing and the restricted range for analytics, since the private range excludes Maps APIs
Use restricted.googleapis.com for all on-premises resolvers, since the stricter range also reaches the Google Maps Platform APIs
Use the restricted range for regulated resolvers and the private range for marketing resolvers, each in its own DNS scope
Use private.googleapis.com for all on-premises resolvers and rely on a VPC Service Controls perimeter to block unsupported services

stem: To remove an exfiltration path, a network engineer deleted the default 0.0.0.0/0 route from a VPC network that hosts private VMs with no external IP addresses. Since then, those VMs can no longer call Google APIs, even though DNS already maps googleapis.com names to the restricted.googleapis.com addresses. What is the minimal change that keeps the internet closed while restoring API access?

choices.text: Create a Cloud NAT gateway for the subnets so that the VMs can reach Google APIs through translated source addresses
Add a custom static route for the restricted.googleapis.com range whose next hop is the default internet gateway
Re-create the 0.0.0.0/0 route and add an egress deny firewall rule for everything except Google API names
Add a VPC Network Peering connection to the Google services network so that API requests travel as internal traffic

stem: A bank wants each business unit's workloads and its on-premises data center to reach Cloud Storage and BigQuery using internal IP addresses that the bank allocates itself, with a separate endpoint per unit so network teams can steer, monitor and prove that traffic stays inside Google Cloud. Which feature fits best?

choices.text: Direct peering with Google, which exposes Cloud Storage and BigQuery on the bank's own address space
Private Google Access enabled on the subnets, because it assigns a dedicated internal address from the bank's range per business unit
A Cloud NAT gateway per business unit, which gives each unit its own translated address for outbound calls to Google APIs
Private Service Connect endpoints for Google APIs, using the vpc-sc API bundle for regulated units, with DNS names that map to each endpoint

stem: An engineer creates a Private Service Connect endpoint named logs1 for Google APIs with the all-apis bundle and expects VMs to call storage-logs1.p.googleapis.com privately. A packet capture shows the traffic going to public Google addresses. The endpoint's forwarding rule is healthy and the VMs have no external IP addresses. What most likely explains this?

choices.text: Endpoints can only be reached from the same region as the forwarding rule, and the VMs run in another region
Private Service Connect for Google APIs needs a peering connection to the Google services network before DNS names work
The VMs resolve the name where no private zone has it, so public DNS wildcard answers return public addresses
The all-apis bundle sends traffic to public front ends unless subnets also have Private Google Access on

stem: A SaaS vendor publishes a managed service behind a Private Service Connect service attachment that explicitly accepts connections only from approved customer projects. A new customer creates an endpoint in its VPC network that targets the attachment, but the connection stays in the Pending state indefinitely. What should the vendor check first?

choices.text: Whether the customer's endpoint uses the same Service Directory namespace as the vendor's published service
Whether the customer's project is on the accept list and whether connection capacity remains
Whether a VPC Network Peering connection exists between the two VPC networks
Whether the customer's subnet range overlaps with the vendor's NAT subnet and must be renumbered

stem: A healthcare company publishes records through a regional managed service that it accesses via Private Service Connect. The security team wants to terminate TLS on its own certificate and domain in front of the service, apply Cloud Armor and centralised logging to the traffic, and fail over between two regions under its own control. Which Private Service Connect type should it use?

choices.text: Private Service Connect backends, using network endpoint groups behind an internal or external Application Load Balancer
Private Service Connect interfaces, because they let the consumer terminate certificates for the producer's service
Private services access, because its allocated range provides load balancer features for managed services
Private Service Connect endpoints, because a forwarding rule gives the same control over certificates and fail over

stem: A retailer connects its data center to Google Cloud with Dedicated Interconnect. A new policy says all traffic between on-premises networks and VPC networks must be encrypted at the network layer from end to end, not only on the physical link. Which design meets this?

choices.text: HA VPN over Cloud Interconnect, with IPsec tunnels established over the VLAN attachments
MACsec on the Interconnect circuit alone, since it encrypts traffic between the two networks
A second Dedicated Interconnect connection in another metro, since redundant circuits encrypt each path
TLS on the application load balancers, since it encrypts all packets in the VPC network at layer 3

stem: A network architect is reviewing MACsec for Cloud Interconnect for a Dedicated Interconnect link and a Partner Interconnect link. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: MACsec encrypts traffic all the way to the VM in the VPC network, inside Google's network too
On Partner Interconnect, the customer should work with the service provider so traffic is encrypted through the provider's network
Enabling MACsec makes IPsec and TLS redundant, so Google recommends dropping them
MACsec establishes IPsec tunnels that terminate on a Cloud Router in the VPC network
MACsec encrypts traffic between the on-premises router and Google's edge router

stem: On-premises hosts in the Frankfurt region reach Google APIs through the restricted VIP over two VLAN attachments that connect to a VPC network. Requests leave the data center, but responses never arrive. The routes to the on-premises networks learned in the VPC network have next hops on a Cloud VPN tunnel and a VLAN attachment, both in a different region than the one the requests entered. What is the likely cause?

choices.text: The Cloud Router advertises the restricted range with a higher MED, so Google drops the requests
The restricted range is only reachable from on-premises IPv6 hosts, which Frankfurt does not use
VPC firewall rules have an implied deny egress rule that blocks all replies to the on-premises network
The next hop toward on-premises is in another region than the request origin, so responses cannot return

stem: A company has private build VMs in a subnet and sensitive data-processing VMs in another, and none of the VMs has an external IP address. Only the build VMs may download packages from the internet, and the security team wants no other VM to be able to initiate internet connections. What is the best design?

choices.text: Place a Cloud Router in the sensitive subnet, because it filters outbound connections by the source VM
Configure a Cloud NAT gateway that serves all subnets in the region, then add a firewall rule to block the sensitive VMs from using it
Configure a Cloud NAT gateway serving only the build subnet, and give the sensitive subnet no NAT and no external IPs
Give the build VMs external IP addresses, because Cloud NAT cannot be limited to a subset of a VPC network

stem: A partner reports suspicious scanning from one of the retailer's shared Cloud NAT external IP addresses. Hundreds of private VMs use that gateway, and the security team must work out which VM made the connections, using the gateway's records. What should have been configured on the gateway?

choices.text: Cloud NAT logging of translations, recording each connection with its internal VM and external address
A larger set of external IP addresses, because each VM then receives its own address that identifies it uniquely
Cloud NAT logging for errors only, because dropped packets reveal every VM that opened a connection
VPC flow logs only on the Cloud Router, because the router records the NAT translations

stem: A consortium member's VPC network is peered with a partner's VPC network so a reporting application can reach one subnet, subnet-a. A second subnet, subnet-b, in the same VPC network holds regulated data and must stay unreachable from the partner. The partner's address ranges are known. What is the right control?

choices.text: A route filter on the peering connection that excludes subnet-b from the routes exchanged
Network tags on the partner's VMs matching tags in the member's ingress rules so only tagged VMs reach subnet-a
Firewall rules created by the partner's administrators, because peered networks apply each other's firewall rules to incoming traffic
Ingress rules in the member's own network allowing the partner ranges only to subnet-a targets, with implied deny for subnet-b

stem: A security architect is reviewing how a Cloud NAT gateway for Public NAT behaves before approving it for private workloads. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Internet hosts can open new connections to a private VM through the gateway's external address once a source port is allocated
Each external address of the gateway is bound to one VM, so a remote party can tell from the address which VM connected
The gateway is a distributed, software-defined service configured on a Cloud Router, with no proxy VMs in the traffic path
Cloud NAT must be configured before VMs can reach Google APIs through the restricted.googleapis.com virtual IP range
The gateway translates only the subnets or subnet ranges selected for it, so VMs in other subnets of the region get no NAT from it

stem: A platform team runs a Shared VPC with one host project and many service projects. The security team wants to ensure that no team can attach its project to a host project outside the approved one, and that each team can place VMs and load balancers only in the shared subnets assigned to it. Which controls should be used?

choices.text: One organization-wide Compute Network User grant to all developers, with firewall rules limiting each team
Org policy constraints on allowed host projects and usable subnets, plus subnet-level Compute Network User grants
VPC Network Peering between each service project's own VPC network and the host project's network instead of Shared VPC
Giving each service project administrator the Shared VPC Admin role, so they can manage their own subnet assignments

stem: A team connects workloads to a managed Cloud SQL instance. It currently uses private services access, which allocates an IP range and peers with the Google-managed producer network. The security team now wants a design where the instance appears at an IP address chosen from the consumer subnet, each consumer project has its own connection, and on-premises clients reach the instance over a hybrid link without extra custom route export. What should the team use?

choices.text: Cloud NAT, which translates the instance's address for the on-premises clients
Private Service Connect for Cloud SQL, with an endpoint in a consumer subnet
A Private Google Access setting on the subnet, which lets Cloud SQL be reached by internal IP
Another private services access range, with custom routes exported on the peering to on premises

stem: A security engineer lists requirements for letting on-premises hosts reach Google APIs privately over Cloud VPN or VLAN attachments with Private Google Access for on-premises hosts. Which TWO items are required? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A Cloud NAT gateway in the VPC network that translates the on-premises hosts' addresses
A Compute Engine VM in every subnet that acts as a forwarding proxy for API calls
An external IP address on every on-premises host that calls the API, so Google can verify the source of requests
Routes for the chosen address range in both the on-premises network and the VPC network, so traffic enters the tunnel or attachment
On-premises DNS records resolving API names to the private.googleapis.com or restricted.googleapis.com addresses

stem: A car insurer lets customers upload photos of driver's licences and claim forms to Cloud Storage. Before sending images to a third-party damage-assessment team, the insurer must obscure names, licence numbers and addresses printed in the images, and hide any visible licence plates. Which approach meets this?

choices.text: Use character masking transformations on the image files, replacing characters in the picture with asterisks
Run a discovery scan configuration, which blurs sensitive areas in images in the bucket after profiling
Use image redaction with infoTypes for text and licence plate objects, and share the returned redacted images
Encrypt the images with a customer-managed key, so the third party sees only ciphertext of the sensitive areas of each picture

stem: A security team wants to be told when a BigQuery table in any of 400 projects becomes more sensitive than before, for example because a new column now holds national ID numbers, and wants high-risk findings to appear next to other issues in its central security tooling. Which setup meets this?

choices.text: Create an organization-level discovery scan configuration with actions for Security Command Center and Pub/Sub on sensitivity changes
Use Data Access audit logs to find which columns are read, and treat frequently read columns as sensitive
Schedule inspection jobs on each table nightly, and write the findings to a spreadsheet for the team to review
Apply a de-identification template to every table, so all columns are treated as sensitive regardless of their real content

stem: A data governance lead is evaluating Sensitive Data Protection discovery for BigQuery and Cloud SQL. Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Discovery requires each table to be exported to a dedicated Cloud Storage bucket before profiling
Profiling BigQuery data generates a table data profile, column data profiles and a project data profile
Discovery profiles only the data in the project in which the scan configuration was created
Discovery automatically masks the detected columns so that analysts see only asterisks
Discovery can send profile results to Security Command Center, and can notify via Pub/Sub when sensitivity changes

stem: A pipeline tokenizes customer IDs with Sensitive Data Protection using deterministic encryption and a transient key. A month later, a compliance team must re-identify some IDs from archived tokens, but the re-identification fails, and tokens created on different days do not match for the same customer. What should have been done?

choices.text: Use a key wrapped by Cloud KMS, keep it available to the re-identifying service, and use the same key for every run
Increase the likelihood threshold of the inspection, so that the tokenized values are recognised on re-identification
Switch to cryptographic hashing, because hashed tokens can be re-identified using the original key
Add a surrogate annotation to the tokens, because that restores the key used to create them

stem: A customer-service platform stores email addresses of very different lengths and containing any characters in a BigQuery column. Analysts must be able to join records for the same customer, and a privileged service must be able to reverse the tokens later. Which transformation fits best?

choices.text: Pseudonymization with format preserving encryption, using the numeric alphabet
Pseudonymization with cryptographic hashing, which is reversible with the original key
Pseudonymization with deterministic encryption using AES-SIV and a Cloud KMS wrapped key
Redaction of the email column, with a copy of the original values kept in a second dataset

stem: A marketing platform tokenizes email addresses so that the same person can be linked within a single campaign but must not be linkable across different campaigns by anyone holding the data. Which Sensitive Data Protection setting achieves this?

choices.text: Turn on a surrogate annotation using the campaign name, because that annotation changes the encrypted value itself
Use bucketing on the email column with one range per campaign
Use a different transient key per API request, so tokens never repeat across requests
Use a context tweak that references the campaign ID column when applying deterministic or format preserving encryption

stem: A team de-identifies free-text chat transcripts with deterministic encryption, replacing detected phone numbers with tokens. Later, a re-identification request on the transcripts returns the tokens unchanged, although the right key is used. What was missing at de-identification time?

choices.text: A larger set of infoTypes in the inspection, because additional detectors let the service reverse any token it finds
A masking character configuration, since masked tokens can be reversed by the key
A surrogate annotation on the tokens, which unstructured text needs to locate and reverse them
A bucketing range on the phone numbers, because ranges are needed to find them again

stem: A privacy engineer must choose transformations that an authorised pipeline can later reverse to restore original values. Which TWO Sensitive Data Protection transformations support re-identification? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Pseudonymization with cryptographic hashing (HMAC-SHA-256)
Pseudonymization with format preserving encryption (FPE-FFX)
Redaction of the detected value
Character masking of the value with an asterisk
Pseudonymization with deterministic encryption using AES-SIV

stem: A platform team stores API credentials in the environment variables of Cloud Run services across many projects. The security team wants to learn about secrets stored there without moving them into every team's own tooling. Which capability helps?

choices.text: Image redaction in Sensitive Data Protection, which scans the container environment variable text for any secrets inside
Cloud NAT logging, which records the secret values leaving the services over translated connections
Private Service Connect backends, which scan the traffic from the services for credential patterns
Sensitive Data Protection discovery, detecting secrets in Cloud Run environment variables and sending findings to Security Command Center

stem: An inspection of support tickets flags many order numbers like ORD-48213 as national ID numbers, creating noise, while internal employee codes in a custom format are never found. What should the security engineer change in the inspection configuration?

choices.text: Add a custom regex infoType for the employee code and an exclusion rule for the order-number pattern in the inspection ruleset
Lower the minimum likelihood to the lowest level, so more candidate matches are returned and the noise disappears
Run the scan as a discovery configuration, which ignores any strings that are not found in a built-in infoType
Switch to cryptographic hashing so that all numeric strings in the tickets are replaced by uniform tokens

stem: After a data-handling incident, an auditor asks the security engineer: "Which principals, including members of nested groups, can read objects in the bucket that holds customer exports, and through which role bindings?" The bucket sits in one project of a large organization. Which Policy Intelligence tool answers this most directly?

choices.text: Policy Troubleshooter, run once for each user in the directory against the bucket and the read permission
Policy Analyzer for allow policies, with the bucket as the resource and the storage read permission as the access in the query
Organization Policy dry-run mode, applied to a storage constraint on the folder that contains the project
IAM recommender, reviewing the role recommendations and policy insights generated for the project and the principals that hold roles on it

stem: A developer in a regulated project reports "permission denied" when reading a BigQuery table, although the group the developer belongs to appears in a project-level allow policy with a suitable role. The security engineer suspects another policy type is involved but cannot tell which. Which approach pinpoints the cause?

choices.text: Put the relevant organization policy constraint into dry-run mode, retry the table read and read the audit logs to see which constraint rejected it
Run Policy Analyzer for allow policies on the project, since its results also include deny policies and boundaries
Run Policy Troubleshooter for that principal, the table and the permission, and read which allow, deny or Principal Access Boundary policy decides the result
Open the IAM recommender insights for the group, because an unused-permission insight explains why a specific request was rejected

stem: A security team applies IAM recommender suggestions to remove roles from engineers. Leadership asks how safe it is to apply them without review. A new on-call role was granted to a service team 3 weeks ago, and a quarterly disaster-recovery role is used only during the drill. What is the right way to handle the recommendations?

choices.text: Review them before applying, since usage is measured over about 90 days, so a recently granted role has little history and a rarely used role may be flagged
Apply all of them at once, because the recommender only flags permissions that are proven by audit logs to be unneeded for any workload
Ignore any recommendation for roles granted at folder or organization level, because the recommender only evaluates roles that are granted on single projects
Apply them only after the recommender converts every flagged role into a custom role, since it cannot suggest predefined role replacements

stem: A company with 300 projects will host regulated workloads (needing a tighter set of constraints) next to standard workloads. Developers must still manage their own projects. Platform engineers want organization policies and IAM grants to be applied once and automatically cover new projects. Which hierarchy design fits?

choices.text: Folders organized only by billing account, with a policy set on each project because folders cannot carry organization policies
A flat list of projects under the organization, with a deployment pipeline that applies its own copy of each constraint and role grant to every project
A separate organization resource for each business unit, so that policies never need to be inherited by child resources at all
Folders for regulated and standard workloads, each with environment subfolders, with constraints and IAM set on folders so that new projects inherit them

stem: The constraint policy for allowed external identity domains is set at the organization with a list of two approved partner domains. A folder for a new joint venture needs a third domain for its projects only, and the other two domains must remain allowed there. The policy is a list constraint. How should the policy at the folder be defined?

choices.text: Edit the organization policy to add the third domain, because child policies can only narrow what the parent allowed
Set the third domain on every project in the folder, because folder policies cannot add values to an inherited list
Set a folder policy that inherits from the parent and adds the third domain, so the effective allowed list is the union
Set a folder policy that does not inherit from the parent and lists only the third domain, because lists always merge anyway

stem: At the organization, a list constraint policy allows two values. A folder below it has a policy that sets inheritFromParent to false and allows one different value. Projects in that folder set no policy of their own. Which TWO statements about the effective policy for those projects are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The folder policy is rejected unless it also repeats the organization's two values, since a list policy must include every ancestor value
The organization's two values are merged with the folder's value, because a child policy has no way to opt out of its ancestors
The projects fall back to the constraint default, because only a policy set directly on a project is evaluated for that project
Only the folder's own value is allowed, because the organization's two values are not inherited by a policy that turns inheritance off
If the folder policy had used restoreDefault with inheritance off, the constraint's default behavior would apply to those projects

stem: A security engineer finds that a constraint (managed by Google with a default of DENY at the organization level) is not being enforced the way she expected. She sets a project under the organization to allow a specific service account, and the effective policy at that project allows it. A colleague claims it should stay DENY, because "deny always wins when policies are merged". What explains the result?

choices.text: The default behavior of a constraint is never merged, so a policy set at the project replaces the default instead of being reconciled with it
The project is exempt from inherited constraints, since projects are the leaf nodes of the hierarchy and cannot receive enforcement
The organization policy service ignored the deny, because default values are written as policies at the organization and expire after a day
A deny only wins when the project and the organization are in different regions, so the allow takes precedence for a global resource

stem: A security team plans to enforce a new constraint across 40 production projects that blocks creation of resources in non-approved locations. Teams fear that automation might break. The team wants evidence of what would be blocked before enforcement, with no change to behavior. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Enforce it in production and rely on a project owner to remove the policy for any team that breaks
Create the policy in dry-run mode, review the audit-logged violations, then enforce it
Use Policy Analyzer for allow policies to preview which creation requests the constraint will deny
Enforce it only on a single test folder and wait for failures, then expand the scope gradually

stem: Which TWO statements about custom organization policy constraints are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Custom constraints are enforced through the IAM deny policy engine, so no organization policy is created or needed
A constraint using the allow action permits only requests that match its condition, so every other request is blocked
Once a custom constraint is created, it retroactively blocks and deletes resources that already violate it
A custom constraint can be defined for any Google Cloud resource type, including those with no organization policy support
A condition is written as a CEL expression over fields of a supported resource type, such as a node pool setting

stem: One folder holds both development and production-like projects. A security team wants a storage constraint enforced only on resources that are tagged environment=production, without moving projects to separate folders. What is the best way?

choices.text: Create a second organization with production projects, because constraints cannot be scoped by resource attributes
Grant the production team a deny policy on the storage permission, because deny policies and constraints are the same control
Add a conditional rule to the organization policy that enforces the constraint only where the resource carries the matching tag
Use network tags on VMs and reference them in the constraint, since network tags drive organization policy scoping

stem: A central team administers organization policy. A regional IT lead should manage organization policies only for the projects of one region, and must not be able to alter policies elsewhere. The projects carry a region tag. Which design meets this?

choices.text: Grant Organization Policy Administrator unconditionally to the lead, then ask them to avoid editing other regions' projects
Share the credentials of the central team's administrator account with the lead, then remove them after each change
Grant Project Owner on each regional project, since owners may edit any organization policy that applies to their project
Grant Organization Policy Administrator at the organization with an IAM condition that limits it to resources with the region tag

stem: A project is moved from the Sandbox folder to the Production folder. Production has an organization policy that denies external IP addresses on VMs, and Sandbox did not. After the move, a deployment that used to work fails. What is the likely explanation?

choices.text: The project now inherits the Production folder's policies, so its effective policy changed and the new constraint blocks the deployment
The move did not change anything, because policies are copied to a project at creation time and stay fixed after that
Projects keep the policy of their original folder until the old folder is deleted, so the failure must come from something else
The policy applies only to projects that were created in Production, so a moved project is immune and the cause is unrelated

stem: An organization restricts resource locations to the United States. Google adds new US regions over time, and the security team does not want to edit the policy for each new region while all non-US locations stay blocked. How should the allowed values be written?

choices.text: List every current US region and multi-region by name, then revise the list whenever a new region opens
Use the in: prefix with a Google-curated value group such as in:us-locations as the allowed value
Define a custom constraint whose CEL condition lists the US region names, so that it updates itself as regions open
Put each non-US region into denied_values by name so that any newly opened US region is allowed by default

stem: A security engineer plans Cloud NGFW features for workloads. Which TWO of the requirements need the Cloud NGFW Enterprise tier rather than the Standard tier? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Block egress to specific websites by filtering on domain names and SNI values
Allow egress to a named domain by using a fully qualified domain name object in a rule
Deny traffic from IP ranges that threat intelligence marks as malicious
Match traffic with the five-tuple of IP ranges, ports and protocols in a policy rule
Detect and block malware, spyware and exploit traffic by Layer 7 inspection with threat signatures

stem: A security team wants Layer 7 threat inspection of east-west traffic between VMs in a VPC network in two zones of one region, by using Cloud NGFW. Which set of building blocks is required?

choices.text: Packet Mirroring to a collector, with the VPC firewall rules set to block when the collector reports a threat signature
A Cloud Armor security policy attached to the backend service of each VM tier and set to the preconfigured threat rules
One firewall endpoint in a single zone that inspects the whole region, plus network tags on each VM to select what is scanned
A threat-prevention profile in a profile group, an endpoint in each zone, and rules that apply the group

stem: Egress to a SaaS site must be blocked by hostname for workloads in a private VPC. Cloud NGFW URL filtering is configured, but the policy only blocks the exact host name in the clientHello and the team also wants it to catch cases where the HTTPS host header differs. The traffic is HTTPS and no TLS inspection is configured. What explains the limit, and what is the fix?

choices.text: The service matches by destination IP only, so replace the profile with an address group that lists the SaaS IP ranges
The service always decrypts encrypted traffic, so the mismatch is caused by DNS caching and a longer cache lifetime is the fix
Without TLS inspection the service matches only the SNI of encrypted traffic, so enable TLS inspection to let it read the host header
URL filtering supports only unencrypted HTTP, so move the workloads to plaintext connections for the service to work

stem: A bank enables Cloud NGFW TLS inspection in two regions to scan outbound HTTPS from application VMs. After rollout, some clients report certificate errors for inspected sites. What should the engineer check or do?

choices.text: Replace the policy with a single global TLS inspection policy, because regional policies cannot be attached to endpoints
Disable the firewall endpoint's zone association, because inspected sites present a certificate that clients can never validate
Import every destination site's private key into Certificate Authority Service so the certificates match the originals
Create a CA pool and TLS inspection policy in each region, and make clients trust the root CA that signs the inspection certificates

stem: A media site serves images through a global external Application Load Balancer with Cloud CDN enabled. A backend security policy with WAF rules is already attached to the backend service. Requests from one abusive IP range must be rejected even when the response could be served from the cache. What should the engineer add?

choices.text: Identity-Aware Proxy on the backend service, because IAP runs ahead of the cache and refuses unknown addresses
A Cloud Armor edge security policy with a deny rule for the range, attached to the Cloud CDN-enabled backend service
A further deny rule in the existing backend security policy, which sees every request before the cache answers it
A VPC firewall rule on the origin VMs that denies the range, which also stops the cache from serving that range

stem: A nightly job on a Compute Engine VM must call an internal API published through an external Application Load Balancer with Identity-Aware Proxy enabled. No person is signed in when the job runs. Which TWO items let the job authenticate and be authorized? (Select TWO)

choices.text: An employee's browser session cookie kept in Secret Manager and replayed by the job, which IAP treats like a signed-in user
The VM's external address added to an IAP allow list on the backend service, because IAP admits non-interactive callers by source address
A Google-issued OIDC ID token for the IAP-secured resource, sent by the job in the Authorization header
The IAP-secured Tunnel User role for the job's service account, because tunnels carry HTTPS calls to IAP-protected applications
A dedicated service account for the job that holds the IAP-secured Web App User role on the IAP-secured resource

stem: An internal web application behind an external Application Load Balancer has IAP enabled. A penetration test reaches the application without any sign-in by calling a backend VM's external address directly. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Restrict backend firewall rules to the load balancer and health check ranges, and have the application verify the signed IAP header
Turn off IAP on the load balancer, and rely on application-level login for every backend because IAP cannot protect backends
Enable SSL policy minimum TLS 1.2 on the load balancer, which blocks all direct requests to backend VM addresses
Add the tester's address range to the Cloud Armor allow list, since IAP only checks requests that match an allow rule

stem: Contractors and employees use the same internal web portal behind IAP. Only employees may open it, and the lists change often. What is the most maintainable access model?

choices.text: Grant the Project Viewer role to employees, since it automatically unlocks every IAP-secured application
Grant the role to each employee by email address on the backend, because group grants are not supported by IAP
Grant the role to allUsers, then restrict the contractors with a Cloud Armor rule based on their e-mail domain
Grant the IAP-secured Web App User role on the portal's backend to an employees group managed in the identity provider

stem: A compliance review says clients must negotiate at least TLS 1.2 with a global external Application Load Balancer, with a restricted cipher set. The load balancer currently has no SSL policy, and backends speak their own protocol versions. What should the engineer configure?

choices.text: Create a Cloud Armor rule that rejects TLS versions below 1.2, since Cloud Armor filters on the protocol version
Attach an SSL policy using the RESTRICTED profile with a minimum TLS version of 1.2 to the target HTTPS proxy
Leave the default, because a load balancer without an SSL policy uses the MODERN profile with TLS 1.2 as its minimum
Set the minimum TLS version on each backend VM, because SSL policies apply to the connection from load balancer to backend

stem: A SaaS company terminates HTTPS for thousands of customer domains on one global external Application Load Balancer. Certificates are renewed often and the team wants central management at scale. What should the engineer use?

choices.text: Backend VMs terminating TLS themselves, with the load balancer passing encrypted traffic through
Compute Engine SSL certificates attached directly to the target proxy, one per customer domain
Certificate Manager with a certificate map referenced by the target HTTPS proxy
One wildcard certificate for the company's own domain, installed on the proxy for every customer

stem: A company needs a private CA hierarchy for mTLS between microservices and for issuing subordinate CAs to business units. Some certificates must be revocable. Which Certificate Authority Service choice fits?

choices.text: Enterprise tier CA pools for the root and subordinate CAs, since the DevOps tier does not support revocation
DevOps tier pools everywhere, because it is recommended for issuing CAs that need revocation lists
A public CA from a browser-trusted vendor, since private CAs cannot sign internal service certificates
Self-signed certificates created in each service, with the keys in the VM metadata for rotation

stem: A company has an offline, on-premises root CA under strict custody rules. It wants CA Service to issue workload certificates for Google Cloud services that chain to that root, with signing keys protected in hardware. What is the recommended design?

choices.text: Create subordinate CAs in CA Service that chain to the external root, using Cloud HSM-protected keys
Move the root's private key into a Cloud Storage bucket with uniform access, so that CA Service can sign directly
Import the root CA and every certificate it ever issued into CA Service, so that the whole history is stored there
Create a new unrelated root CA in CA Service and tell clients to trust both roots permanently

stem: A team enables a new Cloud Armor rule using the OWASP-based preconfigured SQL injection rule set on a production policy. Last time, a false positive blocked legitimate checkout requests. How should the rule be introduced?

choices.text: Add it to the backend bucket instead of the backend service, which makes rules advisory by design
Add the rule in preview mode, review the logged matches, tune sensitivity or exclusions, then enforce
Enforce it for a day, then delete it if the support queue grows
Add it at the lowest priority so it can only match requests that no other rule matched

stem: A login endpoint behind a global external Application Load Balancer suffers credential-stuffing from many rotating addresses behind shared client-side proxies, which send the true client address in X-Forwarded-For. The team wants to slow and then temporarily block abusive clients without affecting others. Which Cloud Armor design fits?

choices.text: A throttle rule keyed on ALL, so that every client shares one global request budget
A rule that denies all requests from the countries of the largest traffic share
An internal-only service rate limit on the backend, since edge rate limiting cannot see client IP
A rate-based ban rule on the login path keyed on the XFF_IP value, with a threshold and ban duration

stem: A media site wants automatic detection of Layer 7 DDoS floods against a service behind a global external Application Load Balancer, with a suggested rule to block the attack signature. What must the team understand about Cloud Armor Adaptive Protection?

choices.text: It trains on Layer 3 volumetric floods only and ignores HTTP request patterns
It is switched on once per project and then blocks suspected attacks by itself, with no rule or review needed on your side
Full alerts with signature and suggested rule need Cloud Armor Enterprise, otherwise only a basic alert is produced
It counts requests served from Cloud CDN, so cache hits are the primary signal

stem: A company enabled SAML single sign-on between its identity provider (IdP) and Cloud Identity. The IdP enforces multi-factor authentication for every user. A review finds that the three super admin accounts still sign in with Cloud Identity passwords and are never challenged by the IdP. Which TWO changes best protect the super admin accounts? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Move the super admin users into a dedicated organizational unit whose SSO profile has single sign-on turned off
Add a network mask to the single sign-on settings so that sign-ins from the office network are sent to the IdP
Ask the IdP team to extend its multi-factor policy to the super admins, since Google redirects every user to the IdP
Turn off 2-step verification for the super admins so that it cannot conflict with the second factor of the IdP
Enforce Google 2-step verification for all super admin users, preferably with security keys

stem: A company uses IdP-initiated SSO. The super admin dana-admin@example.com exists only in Cloud Identity: the IdP has no matching user and the account has no 2-step verification. An IdP operator who can create users is suspected of creating an IdP user with the same email address and signing in as that super admin. Which remedy addresses the root cause?

choices.text: Rename the super admin account every quarter and keep the new name secret from all of the IdP operators and their managers
Keep all Cloud Identity identities, admin accounts included, a subset of the IdP identities, and enforce post-SSO verification for super admins
Remove the password of the super admin account so that only the IdP can authenticate it from now on, including the break-glass case
Set a network mask on the SSO configuration so that sign-ins from the office network are always sent to the IdP

stem: A company provisions Cloud Identity users from its IdP, but the offboarding process only disables the user in the IdP. Weeks after a departure, an audit finds that the former engineer's laptop still holds working gcloud credentials and that the account still receives budget alert emails. Which change fixes the process?

choices.text: Delete the Cloud Identity user in the same minute that the IdP user is disabled, before any retention period applies
Shorten the IdP session to one hour so that the departed engineer's laptop reauthenticates more often
Suspend the matching Cloud Identity user whenever the IdP user is suspended, ending sessions and invalidating tokens
Have administrators remove the departed user's IAM role bindings in every project when HR announces a departure

stem: HR deletes the IdP account when an employee leaves, but the Cloud Identity user is never removed. Months later, a new hire with the same name gets the same primary email in the IdP, signs in to Google, and inherits the former employee's group memberships and files. Compliance also requires keeping a leaver's data for 90 days. What should the lifecycle automation do when a user is deleted in the IdP?

choices.text: Delete the Cloud Identity user immediately, accepting that Google may permanently remove its data
Reset the password of the Cloud Identity user so that the next owner of the address must choose a new one on first login
Leave the Cloud Identity user active but remove it from all groups so that nothing is inherited
Suspend the Cloud Identity user, rename its primary email to a unique obsolete name, and delete it after retention

stem: A company syncs two Active Directory forests into one Cloud Identity account, using one Google Cloud Directory Sync (GCDS) instance per forest. After rollout, each instance suspends the users that the other instance created, and administrators fear that the user configured for GCDS could also be suspended. Which configuration fixes this?

choices.text: Enable two-way synchronization so that each instance reads the users that the other one created back into its own directory
Add exclusion rules for the other forest's users and groups to each instance, and keep domain admins protected from deletion
Move both forests behind one LDAP query by merging their search bases, and remove the deletion policy so that nothing is ever suspended
Set both instances to delete every Google user missing from their own directory, since the other recreates them next run

stem: Access to a documentation project must be granted to everyone whose HR job-role attribute is Technical Writer. Membership must follow the directory attribute automatically as people change role, and the platform team wants to manage the group through the Cloud Identity Groups API without maintaining member lists. Which group type fits?

choices.text: A dynamic group whose membership is defined by a query on the job-role attribute
A locked group, so that only administrators can edit the member list
A standard Google Group whose owners add and remove writers as roles change
Individual IAM bindings for each writer, regenerated by a nightly export from the HR system

stem: The group gcp-network-admins is populated from the IdP, yet group owners also edit it directly in the Admin console. IdP and Cloud Identity memberships have drifted and some people hold network access that the IdP does not list. Which setting prevents this drift?

choices.text: Replace the group with individual IAM bindings that an administrator reviews every quarter
Restrict who may post to the group so that owners can no longer send messages to its members
Lock the group, so that only authorized administrators can change its core attributes and memberships
Convert the group to a dynamic group whose query matches every user in the organizational unit

stem: A company adds a workforce identity pool provider for a public SaaS identity provider that uses one issuer URL for all customer tenants, so that partner staff can sign in with their own accounts. A penetration test shows that a user from an unrelated customer tenant can present a token that the pool accepts. What fixes this?

choices.text: Map google.subject to the email claim so that unrelated tenants produce a different subject
Create a second pool for the same provider and split users between the two pools to dilute the exposure of each pool
Rely on the issuer URL check, since Google verifies that the token was issued by the provider
Add a provider attribute condition that accepts only tokens whose tenant or organization claim matches the company's tenant

stem: A workforce pool maps google.subject to the IdP email attribute. During a rebrand, the IdP team changes every mailbox to a new domain. Afterwards, everyone can still sign in, but each user has lost all access that was granted with principal identifiers for the old addresses. What explains this and what is the lasting fix?

choices.text: Users must reauthenticate once, after which Google rebuilds their old principal identifiers from the audit logs
google.subject is the key in bindings and the mutable email changed it; map an immutable identifier and recreate the grants
The provider was deleted in the rebrand, so engineers should recreate it with the same name
Federated sessions cache the old subject for 24 hours, so the access returns once the cache expires

stem: Users of a workforce pool sign in successfully, except a few who belong to a very large number of IdP groups. The provider maps google.groups to the full groups claim, and those users' sign-in attempts fail. How should the identity architect fix this?

choices.text: Map the same claim to google.subject so that the groups are carried in the user identifier
Request a higher limit for groups per user before the next sign-in attempt
Map only the groups that are used in IAM bindings, with an expression that filters the claim
Switch the failing users to Google passwords by creating them manually in Cloud Identity

stem: Security shortened the Google session length to 8 hours for SSO users, but employees report that they almost never see a login prompt after the session expires. The IdP keeps its own sessions for 30 days. How can security make the shorter session meaningful?

choices.text: Lengthen the Google session to 30 days so that both sessions expire at the same moment
Disable SSO for all users so that Google passwords decide when a prompt appears
Add a network mask to the SSO settings so that expired sessions are verified against office addresses
Set the IdP session shorter than the Google session, so a new Google sign-in forces new IdP authentication

stem: Before rolling out SSO, a company wants to stop employees from creating personal Google accounts with their corporate email addresses, which would create unmanaged accounts later. Which TWO actions follow Google's guidance? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Provision a Cloud Identity user for every employee, using the corporate address as the primary email or as an alias
Disable SSO for all employees until each person has created a personal Google account
Verify a second domain so that corporate addresses cannot be used to sign up
Publish a policy asking staff not to use corporate addresses for consumer accounts and rely on staff compliance
While consumer accounts are still being migrated, filter verification emails sent from the Google sign-up address and hold them for review

stem: A company deploys from GitHub Actions to Google Cloud with Workload Identity Federation. Any workflow in the company's GitHub organization may deploy to the development project, but only the repository payments-infra may deploy to production. All workflows share one provider. Which design enforces this?

choices.text: Bind the production service account to the principal set for the whole organization and rely on developers to keep production workflows in the right repository
Restrict the provider by repository owner, map attribute.repository, and bind the production account to that repository's principal set only
Create a service account key for payments-infra, store it as a repository secret, and use it only in the production workflow
Place the production service account in the development project so that its deployers can also be limited with the development permissions

stem: A project owner created a workload identity pool that trusts an AWS account the owner personally controls and gave it access to a bucket. Security wants to guarantee, for the whole organization and even for project owners, that only two company AWS accounts can ever be trusted by AWS providers. What should the security engineer enforce?

choices.text: A deny rule that prevents all principals from granting Workload Identity User on service accounts in the organization
The service account key creation constraint at the organization, with exceptions only for AWS projects
A restriction on the identity provider URIs that allows only the GitHub issuer for workload identity pools
An organization policy that limits allowed AWS accounts for workload identity pool providers to the two company accounts

stem: A regulated company hosts GitHub Enterprise Server inside its private network. Its OIDC discovery URL is unreachable from the internet and regulations forbid publishing it. Pipelines must deploy to Google Cloud without any service account keys. Which approach works?

choices.text: Create a workforce identity pool so that pipelines sign in like employees using the console
Publish the discovery document through a public load balancer and restrict it by source address
Create a workload identity pool OIDC provider and upload the issuer's JSON Web Key Set directly to it
Store a service account key in Secret Manager and read it from the pipeline runner

stem: A data pipeline on AWS authenticates with Workload Identity Federation and must call a Google API that does not accept federated principals directly. Most other APIs it uses do support direct access. Which design is correct for this workload?

choices.text: Grant the principal set the Workload Identity User role on a service account that holds the roles, and let the workload impersonate it
Create a service account key for the workload and keep it only on the AWS side
Add the federated principal to a Cloud Identity group and bind the group to the roles instead
Grant the needed roles to the principal set directly and retry, since every API accepts federated principals once the pool exists

stem: Workloads on AWS EC2 use Workload Identity Federation with default attribute mapping. An administrator granted access to one federated principal per instance using the subject value, but each time an autoscaling group replaces an instance the access disappears. Which fix scales?

choices.text: Raise the number of principal bindings allowed per policy and keep adding every new instance as it launches
Create a service account key per instance and rotate it whenever the instance is replaced
Switch the provider to a different AWS region so that the instances get stable subject values
Bind a principal set on the assumed role ARN attribute, which stays constant, instead of per-instance subjects

stem: A security team wants new service account keys to expire automatically after seven days, using the key expiry constraint. Which TWO statements about this control are correct? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The constraint replaces the need for the creation prohibition, which can be removed from all projects
Expiry only matters in scopes where key creation is still allowed, since a creation prohibition leaves no new keys to expire
Expiry times only work for keys that were uploaded rather than keys generated by Google
The constraint also revokes every existing key older than seven days when it is enforced at the organization
The expiry applies only to keys created after the constraint is enforced, and existing keys are not affected

stem: Google detected a service account key of billing-export-sa in a public repository and automatically disabled it, because the Service Account Key Exposure Response setting is DISABLE_KEY. The nightly export that uses the key now fails, and a manager asks to turn the setting off. What is the best response?

choices.text: Turn off the response setting organization-wide, because exposed keys are better monitored than disabled
Delete the key and create a replacement that reuses the same private key material so no deployment has to change at all
Move the export to an attached service account or federation, leave the key disabled, then delete it
Re-enable the key permanently once the repository is cleaned, because the exposure has been removed

stem: One exported service account key is shared by two applications on twelve VMs outside Google Cloud, because a vendor product requires keys. After an incident, investigators cannot tell which application or machine made suspicious calls. Which TWO changes improve traceability? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Create a dedicated service account for each application, so that the principal in audit logs identifies the application
Rotate the shared key every day and record each rotation in a ticket
Put the hostname into the description of the service account and rely on administrators to read the description during incidents
Store the shared key in Secret Manager so that reads of the secret are logged for each VM
Create a separate key for each machine, so that audit records name the originating machine

stem: Developers hold the Editor role in sandbox projects that also contain a highly privileged service account. They have no IAM administration permissions, yet a review says Editor can still lead to that account's privileges. What is the risk, and which preventive control addresses it?

choices.text: Editor can read service account keys from Secret Manager, so the control is to move the keys into Cloud Storage
Editor can edit IAM policies in the sandbox, so the control is to remove the Owner role from the organization
Editor can impersonate any service account, so the control is to enable Data Access audit logs on every service
Editor can create service account keys; block key creation and upload by organization policy, which Editor cannot change

stem: A service reads users' calendars through Google Workspace domain-wide delegation. It currently uses a downloaded service account key to sign requests, and the security team has banned keys. How can the service keep delegation without a key?

choices.text: Use an attached service account to call signJwt on a JWT naming the user in sub, then exchange it for a token
Grant the service account the Owner role on the Workspace organization so that it can read calendars
Create an API key for the Calendar API and restrict it to the service's IP address
Replace delegation by sharing every calendar publicly and letting the service read them anonymously

stem: An organization turned on the legacy constraint that stops automatic Editor grants to default service accounts. Auditors still find the Compute Engine default service account holding Editor in new projects; engineers granted it manually when deployment scripts failed. What closes this gap?

choices.text: Grant Organization Policy Administrator to the engineers so that they can request the exception process
Enforce the managed constraint on privileged basic roles for default service accounts, blocking automatic and manual grants
Enforce the legacy automatic-grant constraint again at the folder level, since reapplying it also blocks manual grants
Delete the Compute Engine default service account in every project, since Google recreates it when needed

stem: A shared project holds 140 service accounts and many seem unused. An earlier clean-up deleted one and a script recreated it with the same name, but all of its role bindings were gone and an application failed. How should the team retire accounts safely?

choices.text: Delete the default service accounts first, because Google recreates them with their original bindings if needed
Delete the account immediately and recreate it with the same email, which restores the original bindings
Review recent authentication activity, disable the account, watch for failures, then delete it after a waiting period
Remove every role from the account first and delete it after a week, because roles cannot be restored once removed

stem: A SaaS provider's backend service account can read every customer bucket. When a customer's browser session starts, the backend must hand the browser a short-lived credential that can only read objects in that customer's bucket. There are hundreds of customers. Which solution is the most efficient?

choices.text: Place each customer's bucket in a separate VPC Service Controls perimeter and issue the same broad token to every browser
Exchange the backend's token for a downscoped token with a Credential Access Boundary for that bucket and read access
Add an IAM condition on the backend service account so that it can read only one customer's bucket at a time
Create one service account per customer, grant each access to one bucket, and mint a token for the matching account

stem: A company enforces the constraint that disables service account creation in application projects, so that all identities are managed centrally. Workloads in those projects must still run as service accounts. Which TWO actions complete the design? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Grant the Service Account Admin role at the organization to each application team to speed up provisioning of new accounts
Share one default service account across all application projects through project-level Editor grants
Enforce the constraint that restricts removal of project liens for cross-project service account use, so only organization-level lien holders can remove it
Re-enable service account creation in every application project and ask the teams to follow naming rules
Create the service accounts in a central identity project and allow them to be attached to resources in the application projects

stem: Terraform runs in CI as tf-prod using a downloaded service account key. After an unapproved production change, logs show only tf-prod, and nobody can say which engineer or pipeline run caused it. How should access be redesigned?

choices.text: Remove the key and let named engineers and the federated pipeline impersonate tf-prod with short-lived credentials
Store the key in Secret Manager and rely on the access logs of that secret to identify the engineer who made changes
Issue each engineer a personal copy of the key so that each copy can be tracked by its file name
Rename tf-prod weekly so that logs show which week the change occurred

stem: A deployment pipeline running as deployer-sa must deploy Cloud Run services that run as runtime-sa. Security rejects granting the Service Account User role to deployer-sa at the project level, because it could then run workloads as any service account in that project. What should be granted instead?

choices.text: The Editor role on the organization, so that all deployments are covered by one grant
The Owner role on the project, because it is the only role that permits deploying services
The Service Account Token Creator role on the project, which allows the pipeline to attach any account without further checks
The Service Account User role on runtime-sa only, which grants permission to attach and act as that single account

stem: A bank attaches an SSL policy with a minimum TLS version of 1.2 and the RESTRICTED profile to the target HTTPS proxy of its global external Application Load Balancer. Auditors ask which TLS version clients that connect over HTTP/3 will negotiate with the load balancer.

choices.text: TLS 1.2 with the RESTRICTED cipher suites, because QUIC connections take their cipher list from the attached policy
TLS 1.3, because HTTP/3 runs over QUIC, which uses TLS 1.3 exclusively, so these clients already exceed the 1.2 floor
No TLS version at all, because the RESTRICTED profile does not allow TLS 1.3 and so rejects every QUIC client
Whatever the client offers, down to TLS 1.0, because SSL policies are ignored for QUIC and the minimum is not applied

stem: A security audit finds that two VMs, one in each of two peered VPC networks, exchange database traffic using their external IP addresses because of an old firewall design. The auditor states that this traffic is not covered by Google's automatic network-layer encryption between VMs. What is the most direct remediation?

choices.text: Move the traffic to the VMs' internal IP addresses across the VPC peering, which Google encrypts with session keys
Put Cloud NAT in front of both VMs so that the connection is wrapped in a Google-managed tunnel
Enable customer-managed encryption keys on both VMs' boot disks so that data in motion between the two VMs is protected with the same keys
Apply a Cloud Armor edge policy to the external addresses so that Google authenticates the connection

stem: A bank runs 40 microservices on GKE clusters in two projects. Auditors want every service-to-service call authenticated in both directions, encrypted in transit with certificates that the bank controls, and enforced without changing application code. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: Attach an SSL policy with the RESTRICTED profile to an internal Application Load Balancer in front of each microservice
Rely on ALTS between pods, since Google authenticates every service to service call in its production network
Use Cloud Service Mesh so that sidecar or mesh data planes enforce mutual TLS with bank-controlled certificates
Ask each team to add TLS libraries and a certificate loader to its own code, then audit each repository quarterly

stem: An analytics team standardised on AMD-based machines for a regulated workload. The threat model includes a compromised hypervisor attempting data replay and memory remapping against guest memory, and the team wants attestation reports it can request at any time from the processor. Which Confidential VM technology matches?

choices.text: Customer-managed encryption keys on the boot and data disks, which keep memory contents unreadable to a compromised host
AMD SEV on N2D machines, because it gives the best protection against hypervisor-based attacks of this type
Shielded VM with a virtual TPM, because measured boot also prevents a hypervisor from reading guest memory
AMD SEV-SNP, which adds hardware protections against replay and remapping and supports attestation reports on demand

stem: A payments company has one existing Standard GKE cluster. Only the tokenization pods need memory encryption, and the platform team wants to avoid taking the other 30 workloads onto confidential hardware or rebuilding the cluster. Which option fits?

choices.text: Define a ComputeClass that uses Confidential GKE Nodes and select it only in the tokenization workloads
Create a Binary Authorization policy that requires tokenization images to be attested before they start
Enable Confidential GKE Nodes at the cluster level so every node in the existing cluster is converted in place
Enable Shielded GKE Nodes on the cluster, since secure boot also encrypts workload memory

stem: A bank and an insurer want to train a fraud model on the union of their customer records. Neither party will let the other see raw records, and neither trusts the cloud operator running the job. Each wants its data key released only to a workload image that both parties have approved. Which design fits?

choices.text: Copy both datasets into one Cloud Storage bucket in a neutral project, inside a VPC Service Controls perimeter
Run the joint workload in Confidential Space, releasing each party's Cloud KMS key only to attested approved workloads
Have both parties de-identify their records with Sensitive Data Protection and email the files to a shared analyst
Run the job on a Confidential VM, with both parties granting the VM's service account access to their data

stem: Which TWO statements about Confidential VM are accurate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: It prevents the application running inside the VM from leaking data it is authorised to read
It makes encrypting disks with Cloud KMS unnecessary, because the whole VM boundary is encrypted
It supports live migration on every available Confidential Computing technology
It offers attestation, so a relying party can verify the identity and state of the VM before releasing secrets
It encrypts guest memory with hardware-based keys, so data in use is not readable by the hypervisor

stem: A healthcare AI team trains models on GPU instances and holds that the model weights and patient images processed on the GPU must not be visible to the hypervisor or to Google Cloud operators, not just the CPU memory. Which approach extends hardware isolation to the GPU?

choices.text: Use CMEK-encrypted boot disks on the GPU instance, since data loaded onto the GPU is then encrypted in GPU memory too
Use Shielded VM with secure boot, which extends measured boot integrity to the attached GPU and its memory
Use NVIDIA Confidential Computing on a supported GPU machine series, paired with a CPU TEE such as Intel TDX or AMD SEV
Place the GPU instance in a VPC Service Controls perimeter, which encrypts data while it is processed on the GPU

stem: A trading firm moved its risk engine from N2D Confidential VMs running AMD SEV to newer machines using AMD SEV-SNP for stronger hypervisor-attack protection. Since the move, the operations team sees VMs restarting during host maintenance events, which broke long batch runs. What should the security engineer explain and recommend?

choices.text: Confidential VMs never experience host maintenance events, so a separate application bug must be causing the restarts
Replace the VMs with Shielded VM instances, which add the missing live migration while keeping memory encryption
Live migration is available only on AMD SEV with N2D and C3D, so design the batch jobs to tolerate restarts or accept that trade-off
The restarts are a misconfiguration; turning on live migration for the SEV-SNP VMs removes them with no change in protection

stem: A bucket holds audit exports under a locked retention policy of seven years. A lifecycle rule deletes objects whose age exceeds one year. A security engineer is asked what the rule will do to a 13-month-old object.

choices.text: The rule is rejected, because a bucket with a locked policy cannot also hold lifecycle rules
The Delete action does not take effect until the retention policy is fulfilled, and then the rule deletes the object
The object is moved to a colder storage class at 13 months, which satisfies the rule without deleting it
The object is deleted at 13 months, because lifecycle actions override retention policies on the same bucket

stem: A bucket has two lifecycle rules with the same age condition of 365 days: one deletes the object, the other changes the storage class to Archive. A new security analyst wants to know what happens to an object that reaches that age with no hold or retention policy.

choices.text: The Delete action takes precedence, so the object is deleted
Cloud Storage applies the rule that appears first in the configuration
The object is changed to Archive first and deleted only after a second evaluation
Both actions run, so the object is first reclassified and then removed

stem: A federal contractor must use TLS settings intended to meet FIPS 140-3 on its external proxy Network Load Balancer. Which TWO statements about SSL policies are accurate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Choosing the COMPATIBLE profile lets legacy clients negotiate SSL 3.0, which is why it suits broad client populations
The policy is attached to a Cloud Armor security policy, which then rejects handshakes that use suites outside the profile
The policy also applies to the connection between the load balancer and its backends, so backend TLS is covered as well
The FIPS_202205 profile supports the TLS 1.3 suites with AES-128 and AES-256 GCM, and leaves out the ChaCha20-Poly1305 suite
The policy is associated with the target SSL proxy and governs the client connection, not the connection to the backends

stem: A data-intake bucket receives large sensitive files through multipart uploads. Many uploads fail midway, and the security team finds that the orphaned parts sit in the bucket indefinitely and still hold fragments of sensitive data. Which lifecycle configuration cleans them up?

choices.text: A rule with the AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload action and an age condition, so that stale uploads and their parts are removed
A rule with the Delete action and a daysSinceNoncurrentTime condition, since orphaned parts are noncurrent object versions
A rule with the AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload action combined with a numNewerVersions condition, to target only leftover parts
A rule with the SetStorageClass action that moves objects to Archive after a week, so the orphaned parts are no longer accessible

stem: A health insurer trains models on Agent Platform. Its security team worries that, with stolen valid credentials, someone could pull training data or models from outside the corporate network, even though all access already uses Private Service Connect for Google APIs. Which control closes that gap?

choices.text: Enable Cloud Armor on the Agent Platform endpoint to filter requests from unknown client IP addresses
Add Private Google Access to each subnet, which blocks internet clients from calling the Agent Platform APIs
Include the Agent Platform API in a VPC Service Controls perimeter so that requests from outside it are denied
Switch the Agent Platform service agent to a custom role, which stops a stolen identity from calling the APIs

stem: Two teams share one project for custom training on Agent Platform. By default each training job runs with the project's Custom Code Service Agent. The security engineer finds that team A's jobs can read team B's bucket through that identity. What is the least-privilege fix?

choices.text: Put each team's data in a separate folder and keep using the Custom Code Service Agent with a deny policy on the other team's folder
Create a dedicated user-managed service account per team with only the roles it needs, and attach it to each of that team's training jobs
Ask the teams to export their own user credentials into the training container so that jobs run as each person
Grant the Custom Code Service Agent the storage admin role on both buckets so that access is consistent for everyone

stem: A custom-trained model deployed to an Agent Platform endpoint must read a feature file from a bucket in another project during prediction. The team granted that bucket's read role to the project's Agent Platform service agent, but the prediction container is still denied. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Grant the read role to the Custom Code Service Agent as well, because prediction containers use the same identity as training does
Add the bucket to the training pipeline's service perimeter so that prediction containers inherit its access
Re-run the training job with CMEK so that the prediction container can decrypt and read the bucket
Deploy the model with a user-managed service account that holds the read role, as the default identity cannot be customised

stem: A company enables customer-managed encryption keys for Agent Platform training and wants to document what the keys cover. Which TWO statements are accurate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Batch prediction results are always encrypted with the training job's key, whatever the destination bucket's configuration
Enabling CMEK removes the need to place Agent Platform in a VPC Service Controls perimeter
The key encrypts data on the boot disks of training VMs, including the copy of code, loaded data and temporary local files
For deployed endpoints, in-memory data used for inference is also encrypted with the CMEK
Metadata such as job names, regions and dataset display names is not encrypted with the CMEK and uses Google default encryption

stem: A legal team demands zero data retention for a customer-service assistant built on Gemini in Agent Platform. The assistant stores multi-turn conversations through the Interactions API and uses Grounding with Google Search. Which TWO changes move toward zero data retention? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Enable CMEK on the endpoint, which prevents Google from retaining the prompts that it processes
Use Web Grounding for Enterprise instead of Grounding with Google Search, which keeps logs that cannot be disabled
Rely on Google's training restriction, which also guarantees that prompts are never stored anywhere
Turn off Cloud Audit Logs data access logging for the Agent Platform API so that no prompt content is recorded in the project
Set store to false in Interactions API requests, because it defaults to true and conversations are otherwise stored

stem: A bank puts Model Armor in front of a customer chatbot. The first design uses one template with the Low and above threshold for every filter on both prompts and responses. Customers complain that harmless messages are blocked. What change best balances protection and usability?

choices.text: Split into prompt and response templates and tune each category, starting at Medium and above or High for general safety
Remove Sensitive Data Protection from the template, since PII filters are the main cause of the blocked messages
Keep Low and above everywhere, and tell customers to rephrase, since a false positive is better than a missed detection
Switch every filter to inspect-only, and rely on the chatbot's own system prompt to block unsafe content later

stem: A security architect needs a minimum level of Model Armor protection applied to every AI application across the organization's projects, while letting application teams add stricter filters of their own. Which feature fits?

choices.text: A VPC Service Controls perimeter around Model Armor that limits which projects may send prompts for screening to the service
One shared template that all teams are required to reference by name in their code
An organization policy constraint that blocks all prompts containing a list of banned words
Model Armor floor settings, which set minimum requirements that templates created within the hierarchy must meet

stem: A bank's assistant must detect prompt injection, redact account numbers in model responses, and flag malicious URLs. A developer proposes relying on Gemini's configurable safety filters. Why is that insufficient?

choices.text: Safety filters cannot be configured, so thresholds cannot be tuned to the bank's use case
Safety filters only block harmful categories, so a Model Armor template with Sensitive Data Protection is needed
Safety filters work only on images and video, so text prompts are never checked
